content.title: About
content.content: Grape juice 100% is made from selected grape varieties without added sugar, preservatives or flavorings. The juice retains the natural taste, aroma and nutrients of fresh grapes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grape juice is rich in antioxidants, especially resveratrol found in the skins of dark grapes.
It can be produced from white or dark grapes; dark juice usually has a richer color and flavor.
Traditionally consumed in Mediterranean countries as a refreshing beverage.
Often used in cooking for marinades, sauces, desserts and cocktails.
When stored properly, the juice can keep its quality for up to 12 months.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress and may support heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Supports blood vessels
items.content: Flavonoids improve vessel elasticity and help maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Mostly water, the juice helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Nutrient content
items.content: Contains potassium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without added sugar, natural sugars can raise the glycemic index, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

items.title: Grape allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to grapes or grape juice.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature may irritate the stomach lining in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improper pasteurization can allow microbial growth; choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink chilled as a refreshing beverage, use in smoothies, cocktails, sauces, marinades, or add to oatmeal and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if taste, smell changes or mold appears.

ice-cream-bar-vanilla-chocolate-coated.title: Ice cream bar, vanilla, chocolate coated

content.title: About
content.content: The vanilla ice cream bar coated in dark chocolate is a convenient snack that combines the smooth, creamy taste of vanilla with the bittersweet notes of chocolate. The portion weighs about 50 g and is typically sold in an individual wrapper.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate‑coated ice cream bar appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Vanilla flavor is derived from the seeds of the vanilla orchid, not from artificial additives.
The dark chocolate coating contains at least 70 % cocoa, boosting its antioxidant content.
Bars are often used as a quick post‑workout snack because they provide carbs and a modest amount of protein.
In some countries the bars are sold in mini‑size portions to help control sugar intake.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Both the chocolate coating and the dairy base supply calcium, which is essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Dairy ingredients provide a small amount of vitamin B12, supporting nervous system function.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugars from the ice cream and chocolate quickly replenish glycogen stores after exercise.

items.title: Antioxidants from chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that may reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: The combination of sugar and chocolate stimulates serotonin production, enhancing mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The bar contains a significant amount of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy components may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains casein and whey, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caffeine in chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate contains a small amount of caffeine, which may affect sleep in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Due to its high calorie density, it is recommended to limit consumption to one bar per day.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is ready to eat straight from the wrapper. It can also be sliced and added to ice cream, yogurt, or used as a garnish in desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. For longer storage, keep refrigerated.

content.title: About
content.content: Scalloped potato with fresh meat is a classic baked dish where thin slices of fresh potatoes are layered with tender pieces of meat and baked in a creamy sauce. The result is a comforting, buttery flavor with juicy meat and soft potatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is traditionally assembled in layers, alternating potatoes and meat.
Common meats are beef or pork, but chicken or turkey can also be used.
The creamy sauce is usually made from milk, cream, and flour, giving the dish its smooth texture.
Baking allows the potatoes to fully absorb the flavors of the meat and sauce.
Some regional variations add cheese on top for a golden crust.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide slowly digestible carbs that supply steady energy.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat component delivers complete protein essential for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both potatoes and meat contain B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies potassium, iron, and zinc, which help maintain electrolyte balance and immune health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Potato skins and any added vegetables contribute fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The creamy sauce and meat make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Cream and meat can increase saturated fat intake, which may be a concern for heart health.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Those with dairy sensitivities should substitute cream with plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Added salt in the sauce can be problematic for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, often accompanied by a green salad or vegetable side. Garnish with fresh herbs for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven to retain the crispy top.
